report.source_text: lumbar puncture was performed, along with CSF pathology and NGS examination, which indicated Listeria infection. CSF pathology (severe central nervous system inflammation, predominantly lymphocytes; no Cryptococcus or atypical cells detected. Leukocyte: 394/µL, Neutrophils: 16%, Lymphocytes: 72%, Monocytes: 11%, Plasma cells: 1%). NGS: (G + Listeria: Sequence Number: 3412, Relative Abundance: 95.63%; LM: Sequence Number: 2619; Q30:92.14).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old man presented subacutely with dizziness, nausea, vomiting, followed by fever. Physical examination revealed stiff neck and sluggish light reflex. CSF analysis showed pleocytosis (210 × 10^9/L cells), high protein (1371.5 mg/dL), and low glucose (1.1 mmol/L) indicating CNS infection. Blood culture confirmed Listeria infection two days after fever onset. Brain MRI revealed lesions in the right pontine and brachium pontis consistent with meningoencephalitis. CSF pathology showed severe CNS inflammation predominantly lymphocytes, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified Listeria monocytogenes with high sequence numbers and relative abundance, confirming CNS infection by Listeria.
